name: NY-16
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +18 partisan lean
Incumbent George Latimer running for reelection with a fundraising edge
Republican challenger Joseph Cinquemani has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96%
model.rationale: The district's +18 Democratic lean, Latimer's incumbency and fundraising advantage, and a Republican challenger with no reported campaign finance all point to a comfortable Democratic hold. Markets price this race at roughly 96% Democratic, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against Latimer or an unexpected scandal would be the main way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
NY-16 is a heavily Democratic Westchester-area district where first-term incumbent George Latimer is seeking reelection. The seat's partisan lean of +18 Democratic gives any Republican nominee a steep uphill climb, and Latimer enters the general election as the clear favorite.

Latimer has raised about $514,000 and holds a six-figure war chest, while Republican Joseph Cinquemani has reported no fundraising, limiting his ability to compete in an expensive New York media market. No independent ratings or public polls cover the race, but prediction markets put Democratic win odds near 96%. Barring unforeseen developments, Latimer is positioned to win comfortably.
